newsitem.title: USA: CSX, Conrail amend merger deal.
newsitem.headline: CSX, Conrail amend merger deal.

text.p: CSX Corp and Conrail Inc said on Wednesday they have amended the terms of their merger agreement. Under the revised terms, CSX has raised the cash portion of its offer to $110 per Conrail share.

In an announcement jointly released with CSX, Conrail said its board has considered the relative merits of a merger with Norfolk Southern Corp rather than with CSX and has reaffirmed that a merger with CSX is in Conrail's best interests and is the superior strategic combination for Conrail.

CSX chairman John Snow said in a statement that the company's decision to raise its cash offer reflects a management analysis which identified at least $730 million in synergies and cost savings, $180 million more than it had originally anticipated.

"The hostile Norfolk Southern bid is burdened with a series of significant conditions," Snow said. "Given all the obstacles in the path of Norfolk Southern's bid, Conrail shareholders would have to wait a prolonged amount of time to receive payment for their shares."

The companies said the November 14 Conrail shareholders' meeting has been canceled, and a record date for a new shareholders meeting has been set for December 5, with the meeting expected to be held in mid-December.
Norfolk Southern on Tuesday reaffirmed its all-cash $100 per share offer for Conrail, adding that it has terminated its talks with CSX "because it was a waste of time."

It again released a statement on Wednesday from its chairman David Goode, saying, "We are committed to taking every necessary step to provide Conrail shareholders with the choice of our better offer."

Conrail and CSX said the structure of the proposed merger would remain the same, with 40 percent of the fully diluted shares of Conrail's common stock and ESOP preferred stock to be acquired at the new price and the remaining 60 percent to be exchanged for CSX stock at the original exchange ratio of 1.85619 CSX shares for each Conrail share.
CSX's $110 per share tender offer is for about 17.9 million shares of Conrail common and preferred stock, or about 19.9 percent of the Conrail outstanding voting stock.
Under the amended terms, the tender offer's expiration date and withdrawal and proration rights are extended through November 20, the companies said.
At the close of business on Tuesday, 56,634 Conrail shares had been tendered pursuant to the CSX offer, they said.
They added that the period during which the Conrail board cannot withdraw its support for the merger or agree to any competing deals will be extended by three months, until July 12, 1997.
